patch.value: Accept approved author and committer identities with a trusted forward baseline
Mirror fleet identity controls, diagnose offending commits and roles, and exercise real adversarial Git histories. Release remains held.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Design: approved public emails, not display names; audit author and committer on every reachable commit after the root anchor. Read controls from the trusted default branch after adoption so a PR cannot widen its own allow-list or advance its own baseline. Keep the existing tracked UTF-8 path gate and the release hold.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Revert proof: replacing only scripts/identity.ts with origin/main leaves the new tests unchanged and fails 6 of 7 cases, including approved fleet identities and missing-base refusal. Restoring the implementation passes 7 of 7. Typecheck and docstring gates pass. No tags, publishing or release activation.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Validation: npm run release:check and bun run release:check passed in CI identity environments. Each ran 47 tests with 47 passes, zero failures or skips; all source statements, branches, functions and lines are 100%. Both packed npm and Bun consumer acceptances passed. Linked adversarial tests also passed 7/7. The root anchor covers every later kit and merge commit. Release remains held.

value.text: Round 1 review: fail closed for absent trusted controls; validate proposed controls without activating them; audit both reachable histories with exact emails; isolate merge-committer regression; pin trusted base SHA. Main currently has neither control, so adoption must remain blocked until independently trusted controls exist. Main protection already requires strict verify (22), verify (26), and analyze checks.

The restored identity suite passes 14/14. CodeRabbit replacement/removal of both controls is covered. npm and Bun release:check both fail closed because main has neither trusted control; no bypass or ref rewrite is used.
